text:
dmitri: quick share — ran the fragmentation-aware queue-gating experiment on us-east-1/gpu-pool-2 for 6h. goal was to avoid KV OOMs by rejecting/reshaping batches when per-shard KV fragmentation > 40% and free-seg count < 64. results are mixed.
maya: can you paste the numbers? curious about how you computed fragmentation.
dmitri: sure. summary first: total_reqs=118842, accepted_batches=103124 (86.8%), rejected_by_gating=15678, evicted_kv_entries=214, kv_eviction_rate=0.18%, OOMs_prevented=7 (no customer-impact), p50_lat=32ms, p95_lat=192ms (+18ms vs baseline), p99_lat=420ms (+70ms). kernel_fallback_count=3700 (3.1%).
kevin: kernel_fallback_count up — expected because when we gate we sometimes route to a smaller/quantized kernel path? is that the fallback you're using?
dmitri: yep. heuristic currently does: if (kv_frag_pct > frag_thresh || free_seg < free_thresh) then: reduce batch_token_budget by 30%, switch model variant to quant8_fallback if available, and increase admission-delay by 10ms to let KV drains settle. code snippet:

```
if kv_frag_pct > 0.4 or free_seg_count < 64:
    token_budget *= 0.7
    route.variant = 'quant8_fallback'
    admission_delay_ms += 10
```

maya: how is kv_frag_pct computed? naive fragmentation metrics can be noisy.
dmitri: we compute kv_frag_pct per shard as 1 - (largest_contiguous_free / total_free). we sample every 2s and smooth with ema(α=0.25). free_seg_count is count of contiguous free segments > page_size(4k).
lia: interesting. the p95 bump worries me. looks like the fallback kernel has higher tail latency for short sequences — maybe kernel kernel-selection is mismatching. have you profiled kernel latency for short vs long seqs?
dmitri: yes — attached a short profile (excerpt):

```
kernel_profile: {
  'fused_attn_fp16': p50=28ms p95=170ms p99=360ms
  'fused_attn_int8': p50=35ms p95=210ms p99=480ms
  'fallback_unfused': p50=22ms p95=240ms p99=600ms
}
batch_shape_mix: short_seq(<=64): 62% / medium: 28% / long:10%
```

kevin: looks like quant8_fallback (int8) increases p95 but unfused fallback even worse. maybe we should prefer keeping fused_fp16 for short_seq and only fallback to int8 for long seqs where memory savings matter more. could add a per-batch kernel selection score: score = latency_est + lambda * memory_saving. pick min score.
maya: agree. also the admission_delay might be causing head-of-line blocking for short requests queued behind big ones. maybe change queue policy to prefer reshaping small or short-seq batches when frag_pct high.
dmitri: tried a small change to queue policy: when frag_pct > 0.4, mark large-seq requests as deprioritized and try to fill short_seq batches first. that cut p95_short_seq by ~12ms but increased long-seq p95 by ~35ms (few customers impacted). tradeoff seems okay but we need opt-in per-customer.
oomwatcher-bot: alert — 7 potential OOMs prevented in run 1867500000, no SLA breaches detected.
lia: two practical suggestions: (1) add kernel-selection scoring as kevin suggested (latency_est from perf table, memory_saving from kv footprint estimate); (2) add a small fast-path check: if batch_shape_short_ratio > 0.6 and fused_fp16 is available -> prefer fused_fp16 regardless of frag_pct. this avoids the big tail for majority short traffic.
dmitri: will prototype both. one more ask — does anyone have a quick heuristic for determining when KV fragmentation is transient vs persistent? we want to avoid oscillation (flip-flopping admission thresholds).
kevin: use hysteresis + lease: only flip gating state if frag_pct stays > X for T_stable (e.g., 30s) and require >Y reduction for 60s to open again. also track per-shard trend slope; if slope negative (improving) don't tighten further.
maya: also track rejected_batch_count per-customer — if a single high-QPS customer triggers gating frequently, consider per-customer token limits rather than global gating.
dmitri: great. i'll spin up a canary with kernel-scoring + short-pref queue + hysteresis and run 12h in us-west-2. will post numbers. thanks all :thumbsup:
kevin: :rocket:
lia: :eyes:
